R199-C3_Irreversibility_Boundary_Engine.strongest_102_attack: No single reference found that anticipates 'irreversibility boundary' as a DECISION VARIABLE (distinct from risk/failure-probability) with the four estimated quantities (distance, uncertainty, time-to-crossing, intervention-required). The closest references (Voit 2019, Zoll 2016, stroke time-is-brain) each cover part of the concept but none frames recoverability as a separate decision variable. §102 does NOT kill R199-C3.
R199-C3_Irreversibility_Boundary_Engine.strongest_103_ksr_combination: Likely combination: (causal digital twin, Springer 2026) + (critical transition / tipping point theory, Voit 2019) + (treatment futility / time-is-brain, stroke literature) + (shunt-specific AI, US 20260115436). A PHOSITA might combine these to estimate an irreversibility boundary. HOWEVER, the specific framing — recoverability as a decision variable DISTINCT from risk, with the four estimated quantities — is NOT explicitly taught in any combination. The §103 threat is MODERATE but not dispositive.
R199-C3_Irreversibility_Boundary_Engine.is_the_irreversibility_framing_genuinely: PROBABLY YES — The key distinction is between 'risk' (probability of an adverse event) and 'recoverability' (distance to the point beyond which recovery is impossible). These are genuinely different decision variables. A clinician told 'risk = 68%' makes a different decision than one told 'the patient remains recoverable for 41-63 hours, after which intervention X has substantially lower probability of restoring baseline.' The latter is a TIME-CRITICAL RECOVERABILITY statement, not a risk probability. This framing has not been found in the prior art. The concept of 'treatment window closing' exists in stroke and pharmacology, but it has not been operationalized as a continuous real-time patient-specific boundary estimation with the four quantities R199-C3 proposes.
R199-C3_Irreversibility_Boundary_Engine.rationale: R199-C3 is the STRONGEST candidate of the five. The 'irreversibility boundary' as a decision variable distinct from risk/failure-probability is a genuinely novel conceptual contribution. No single §102 reference anticipates it. The §103 threat is MODERATE (the components exist in separate fields: causal DT, critical transition theory, treatment futility) but the specific integration — recoverability as a real-time monitored decision variable with distance/uncertainty/time-to-crossing/intervention-required — has not been explicitly disclosed. The killer experiment (same ICP/flow/biomarkers but different distances from irreversibility) is genuinely discriminating and has not been demonstrated in the literature. The moat is the recoverability model + longitudinal causal data + intervention-response history, which requires years of data to accumulate. R199-C3 should advance to Level 3 attack (deep §103 obviousness analysis + light simulation of the killer experiment). CAVEAT: This assessment was synthesized due to API rate limits; the §103 threat analysis should be deepened with fresh patent searches when the API is available. The CONVERGING_TECHNOLOGY rule applies: as causal digital twins mature, the irreversibility boundary framing may become obvious by 2028-2030. The moat depends on the recoverability model being non-obvious and the longitudinal data being hard to replicate.
R199-C3_Irreversibility_Boundary_Engine.caveat: This assessment was synthesized from prior art evidence due to persistent web_search API 429 rate limits. The functional-equivalent search (therapeutic window closing, treatment futility, point of no return, tissue viability threshold, no-reflow) was NOT exhaustively executed. There is a MODERATE risk that a more thorough search would find a closer reference. The candidate should be re-verified with fresh searches before committing significant simulation budget.

R199-C4_Self_Identifying_Therapeutic_Sys.strongest_102_attack: US 12,636,471 (programmable CSF metering shunt) teaches closed-loop implanted CSF drainage with measurement -> known-volume removal -> parameter calculation -> adjustment. It does NOT explicitly claim: (a) predicting response BEFORE observing it; (b) comparing predicted to actual; (c) declaring model failure when prediction != reality; (d) automatically re-identifying patient; (e) switching to safe fallback control policy during re-identification. §102 does NOT kill R199-C4.
R199-C4_Self_Identifying_Therapeutic_Sys.strongest_103_ksr_combination: US 12,636,471 (closed-loop shunt) + industrial model-plant mismatch detection (ACS 2025) + safe RL OOD detection (OGSRL NeurIPS). A PHOSITA would be motivated by FDA PCCP guidance to combine these. §103 threat is MODERATE-HIGH. HOWEVER, three non-obvious aspects remain: (1) discrete model-failure declaration vs continuous gradual model updating (iLet); (2) automatic device-initiated re-identification vs clinician-triggered; (3) safe policy switching during re-identification vs mere abstention (H6).
R199-C4_Self_Identifying_Therapeutic_Sys.overlap_with_H6_uncertainty_gated_twin: MODERATE — H6 = pre-action UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION ('if too uncertain, gather more data or abstain'). R199-C4 = post-action MODEL VALIDATION ('my prediction was wrong; model is invalid; re-identify patient; switch policy'). Distinct at the architectural level. A system implementing H6 would naturally evolve toward R199-C4 as the next step after sustained high uncertainty.
R199-C4_Self_Identifying_Therapeutic_Sys.is_model_failure_detection_genuinely_new: PROBABLY YES — The integrated architecture (predict -> observe -> compare -> declare model failure -> automatically re-identify patient -> switch to safe control policy) in an IMPLANTED MEDICAL DEVICE has NOT been found in any single prior-art reference, patent, or commercial product. The closest commercial system (iLet) does lifelong learning but never declares model failure. The closest research system (VIEshunt + safe active learning) does safe learning but not model-failure-aware re-identification. The novelty is at the ARCHITECTURAL level (combining existing components in a new way for a new use case).
R199-C4_Self_Identifying_Therapeutic_Sys.rationale: R199-C4 survives §102 (no anticipatory reference). §103 threat is MODERATE but survivable with narrow claim drafting focused on: (a) implanted medical device context; (b) discrete predict-observe-compare-declare-reidentify-safe-switch architecture; (c) automatic device-initiated re-identification; (d) safe fallback policy switching during re-identification. The candidate is genuinely distinct from H6 at the architectural level. The killer experiment (introduce unmodeled physiological transition; does the controller recognize model failure vs. blindly optimize harder?) is the RIGHT discriminating test and would expose the difference between R199-C4 and commercial adaptive controllers (iLet, BrainSense) that would FAIL this experiment. This non-obvious result would significantly strengthen patentability. The candidate's novelty is ARCHITECTURAL (combining existing components in a new way), not component-level — architectural novelty is harder to defend against §103 but the killer experiment provides concrete evidence of non-obviousness. ADVANCE to Level 3 attack with the killer experiment as the primary simulation target.
R199-C4_Self_Identifying_Therapeutic_Sys.the_general_architecture_potential: The CEO notes this could become a general architecture for shunts, insulin pumps, drug-delivery systems, neurostimulation, ventilators, artificial organs. This BROADENS the commercial value significantly but also BROADENS the prior art exposure (each domain has its own adaptive control literature). Claims should be drafted to cover the specific architecture across implantable therapeutic device classes.

proposed_constitutional_amendment_articl.authority: CEO Round 199: 'Add one new constitutional question: FUTURE-NOVELTY TEST: Could a well-funded 2028 competitor plausibly build this by combining technologies that already exist in 2026? If yes, the candidate is probably not a sufficiently strong invention. The better candidate is: Something whose missing capability requires a new scientific/causal insight, not merely integration of today's components.'
constitutional_basis: Article I — evidence precedes assertion
Article XIX — never optimize for the gate
Article XXVIII — no silent semantic promotion
Article XXXII — state strongest alternative

proposed_constitutional_amendment_articl.the_article_text:
Before a candidate may advance beyond novelty level 2 (NOVELTY_SURVIVES_CURRENT_SEARCH), it must pass the FUTURE-NOVELTY TEST: 'Could a well-funded 2028 competitor plausibly build this by combining technologies that already exist in 2026?' If YES, the candidate is INVENTIVE-STEP THREATENED and may not advance to level 3 (INVENTIVE_STEP_SURVIVES) unless it demonstrates a missing capability that requires a new scientific/causal insight, not merely integration of today's components.

The test is applied as follows:
1. Enumerate the enabling components of the candidate (sensors, algorithms, data sources, models, control architectures).
2. For each component, determine: does this component exist in 2026? (Yes/No/Converging)
3. If ALL components exist or are converging in 2026: the candidate is FUTURE-NOVELTY THREATENED. It may still advance if it demonstrates a NEW DECISION CAPABILITY (a new question the clinician can answer) that is not merely the sum of its components.
4. If ANY component requires a new scientific/causal insight that does not exist in 2026: the candidate is FUTURE-NOVELTY ELIGIBLE.
5. The test is ADVERSARIAL: the coder must construct the strongest 2028-competitor build scenario before assigning novelty level 3+.

This article extends CONVERGING_TECHNOLOGY_NOT_WHITE_SPACE (Round 194) from a static 2026 obviousness test to a dynamic 2028 competitor prediction. The combination is the same warning: converging technology is where competitors will move next, NOT a defensible white space.

the_relationship_to_existing_rules.extends_CONVERGING_TECHNOLOGY_NOT_WHITE_: Round 194 rule asks 'is this converging in 2026?' Article XXXVII asks 'could a 2028 competitor build this from 2026 components?' The latter is a 2-year forward projection of the former.
the_relationship_to_existing_rules.extends_SUCCESSOR_REQUIRED: Round 188 rule prevents V2/V3 rebranding of the same concept. Article XXXVII prevents V1 of a concept that is merely a 2028 competitor prediction.
the_relationship_to_existing_rules.informs_NOVELTY_CONFIDENCE_LEVELS: A candidate that fails the Future-Novelty Test may not advance beyond level 2, regardless of how well it survives the static 2026 §102/§103 search. The test adds a TEMPORAL dimension to novelty assessment.
